qty_break.description: C-037 — the quantity this rate applies from. Carbon quotes per quantity break; a line with no break is a flat rate.
C-037 — the quantity this rate applies from. Carbon quotes per quantity break; a line with no break is a flat rate.

is_inclusive._comment: GST-20. Set from the document's `is_inclusive_tax` by engine/gst.py::apply_item_taxes. It lives on the LINE because `taxable_amount` is a child computed expression and a child cannot see its parent's columns.

taxable_amount.computed: round(amount / (1 + is_inclusive * (cgst_rate + sgst_rate + utgst_rate + igst_rate + cess_rate) / 100), 2)
taxable_amount._comment: GST-20. The value GST is charged on for THIS line, and the figure GSTR-1 table 12 declares per HSN. On an exclusive document it equals `amount`; on an inclusive one the tax is already inside `amount` and is extracted rather than added. The head amounts below read this, not `amount` — computing them on the gross declared 18% more output tax than an inclusive invoice had collected.

fields.name: total_tax
fields.computed: max(sum(taxes.amount), sum(items.cgst_amount) + sum(items.sgst_amount) + sum(items.utgst_amount) + sum(items.igst_amount) + sum(items.cess_amount))

role.description: What this party IS to the business. A school's parent is a `guardian`, not a `customer`; a clinic's referring GP is a `referrer`, not a `partner`. Three agents building school and clinic data had to file parents and GPs as `customer`/`partner` because nothing else fitted — and terminology renames Party to Student, so a mother appeared under a "Student" label.
